question: Identify the correct chemical reaction involved in bleaching powder preparation

options.text: NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 → NH4Cl + NaHCO3
NaHCO3 + H+ → CO2 + H2O + Sodium salt of acid

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O** is the correct chemical reaction for the preparation of bleaching powder.
 
• Bleaching powder, also known as calcium hypochlorite, is widely used for disinfecting drinking water and in the textile industry for bleaching fabrics.
 
• This reaction involves the chlorination of calcium hydroxide, resulting in the formation of bleaching powder and water.
 
• The chemical formula for bleaching powder is Ca(OCl)2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorine** is a powerful oxidizing agent and is used in various industrial and household applications.
 
• Calcium hydroxide, also known as slaked lime, is used in the preparation of bleaching powder due to its alkaline nature.
 
• Bleaching powder should be stored in a dry and cool place to prevent it from decomposing and losing its effectiveness.
 
• It is important to handle bleaching powder with care, as it can be irritating to the skin and eyes and is harmful if inhaled.
